'''''Escallonia rubra''''', called '''redclaws''' and '''red escallonia''', is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Escalloniaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:791101-1 |title=''Escallonia rubra'' (Ruiz & Pav.) Pers. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=18 January 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url=https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3BGHJ |title=Escallonia rubra (Ruiz & Pav.) Pers. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=18 January 2025}}</ref> It is native to southern Chile and neighboring areas of Argentina. 

==Description==
[[File:Escallonia rubra (8674697936).jpg|thumb|left|A variety with narrower leaves and redder petals]]
''Escallonia rubra'' is a spreading shrub usually 0.8 to 1.0{{nbsp}}m tall, but can reach a height of 3.6{{nbsp}}m.<ref>[http://plantselector.botanicgardens.sa.gov.au/Plants/Details/111 ''Escallonia rubra'' Red Escallonia] Plant Selector</ref> It features glossy, elliptical, serrate evergreen leaves. The upper side is glossy and dark green, while the lower side is much lighter. The bark is first red and rough-haired, which later turns brown and dotted, and eventually gray and cracked. The buds are scattered and oval with finely serrated edge on the outer half. The [[root system]] is stringy and somewhat weak in the first years. Later, strong main roots are formed, which lie high in the ground.

The pink to crimson trumpet-shaped flowers bloom in July to October in the Northern Hemisphere. The prominent, maroon to red [[Hypanthium|hypanthia]] are campanulate with acute apices, leading to the common name redclaws. The flowers sit in short clusters from the leaf corners. The [[petal]]s are fused into a short tube. The fruits are capsules.

==Occurrence==
The shrub occurs on the slopes of the [[Andes Mountains]] in [[southern Chile]] and Argentina all the way down to [[Tierra del Fuego]], where it grows in scrub and open forest, among other biomes. 

==Cultivation==
Cultivated as a garden and hedging plant, it has become naturalized in western Europe, Oregon in the United States, and New Zealand, and is considered invasive in places. It is grown in many other areas, such as Australia. Its cultivar 'Crimson Spire' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Escallonia rubra'' 'Crimson Spire' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/55322/i-Escallonia-rubra-i-Crimson-Spire/Details |access-date=6 November 2019}}</ref>
